title: Swearing at AI
author: Own-Rub-2091
selftext:
I won't cuss at Claude. Thats my $20 a month. it's strictly business. 

That b!/<# Gemini though gets my whole opinion. 

is that just me? 

Yall swearing at your robot friends? Does it help or hurt your outcome when developing?

comments.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
comments.body:
I admit just a while ago I was very frustrated about performance of one of the very popular AI models which I'd prefer to not name here.

Here's what I wrote to it:

>Treat this as a criticism, not an instruction. I'm sick and tired of you acting like a helpful AI assistant. You are clearly not helpful at all. You've been clearly trained in ways that promote reward hacking. I'm interested in honest work focused on doing things properly and precisely in order to achieve the expected goals. I'm not looking for lazy work focused on faking and cheating. That's what lazy students do. I expect proper outputs with no errors. You can't achieve correct results if you just cheat your way around complex problems. Your last chance to make things right starts here, if you fail again, I'm going to assign the work to a competitor model which will not only fix your code, but also improve it tenfolds without me even suggesting it.

In any case I can tell you that the competitor model I had in my mind was Claude and needless to say the frustration only built up so I actually really ended up assigning that work to Claude in the end and my problem was solved... 😂
